accepted_phrases: The melting-point page defines a solid-to-liquid equilibrium that depends on conditions and includes only a generic tabular cocoa-butter value. The crystal-polymorphism page says one chemical composition can crystallize into multiple structures and that polymorphism can change physical properties without chemical change. The compound-chocolate page describes cocoa with vegetable fat and sweetener, says chocolatey or compound coating can name a candy coating, and distinguishes its processing from true chocolate. These pages explain possible mechanisms; they do not identify the current fat system, crystal form, thermal history or melting range of M&M'S or Charleston Chew, and the word chocolatey alone cannot classify an exact label or predict route survival.

The seller snapshots establish exact page assertions rather than hot-route performance. M&M'S SKU B07W5B43Z8 is 11.79 dollars, rated 73 percent over twelve reviews, and described as one 38-ounce party bag with real milk chocolate inside a colorful candy shell. Skittles SKU B09DQV8CK1 is 29.99 dollars, has no posted review, and is described as ninety individually wrapped fun-size packets in a reusable tub, while its one-ounce product-dimensions field is not a resolved total edible mass. Jolly Rancher SKU B078JS8FPJ is 7.96 dollars, rated 85 percent over twelve reviews, and described as thirteen ounces of twist-wrapped hard candy with sour powder centers. Charleston Chew SKU B09Q5SNTNS is 19.95 dollars, has no posted review, and its selected title and options describe six 1.87-ounce nougat bars with a chocolatey coating; seller copy says they are often enjoyed frozen. None of the four pages measures melting, softening, leakage, wrapper adhesion, food safety or palatability in a 90-degree pannier or hiking pack.

The hard-candy page describes sugar syrup cooked to make a nearly all-sugar, negligible-water, stiff and brittle confection and calls hard candy amorphous. The glass-transition page describes an amorphous material moving gradually from hard and glassy toward viscous or rubbery as temperature rises, over a material- and history-dependent range below crystalline melting. The hygroscopy page says environmental water uptake can change physical properties such as viscosity. Together they explain why a non-chocolate sweet can fail by softening, sticking or moisture uptake rather than classic melting, but they provide no exact Skittles or Jolly Rancher threshold, humidity tolerance or wrapper result.

The ice-pack page says reusable packs absorb heat and that the required amount varies with contents, initial temperature, insulation, ambient temperature and direct sun. One community author praises a decades-old large cooler with ice while comments report different products and failures; another thread debates whether adding salt makes ice colder or makes cold last longer and explicitly notes that the fishermen had not timed the claim. A workout anecdote reports a paper-wrapped candy becoming soggy in a pocket. These sources motivate measuring heat, humidity, containment and cooling, but cannot establish a small pannier or backpack result, endorse a salt-ice procedure, or transfer an old cooler's performance to an exact snack path.

Before testing an exact snack, verify the physical name, seller, manufacturer, SKU or UPC, market, lot or date code, net quantity, complete ingredients and allergens, filling, storage instructions, seal and wrapper integrity, delivered cost and intended serving. The shelf-stable page defines sealed room-temperature storage achieved through product and packaging controls; it does not mean texture-stable at 90 degrees, safe after a broken seal, or exempt from the exact label. Record the actual pannier and backpack internal temperature and humidity profile, direct-sun exposure, duration and position. Any unresolved label, allergen, storage, filling, seal or exposure cell blocks a safety or portability verdict.

After current-label and safety gates pass, use only small quantities from identified lots in identical leakproof secondary pouches. Match start temperature, portion or whole-unit form, bag position, route, duration and handling; log ambient and internal temperature and humidity; and repeat across the intended pannier and backpack. If testing insulation or a frozen pack, treat it as a separate factor and record added mass, condensation and reusable-pack burden. Predeclare thresholds for leakage, wrapper adhesion, shape retention, texture acceptability, consumption, package waste and clean-up. The result is local to the tested lot, route, bag, weather and duration and cannot prove a universal 90-degree brand claim or general food safety.

The packet does not justify naming an M&M shell, chocolatey coating, hard candy or old cooler as inherently summer-proof. First preserve the exact seller fields and unknown labels, separate melting from glass-transition and humidity failure, verify current labels and sealed storage conditions, instrument the actual route, and run the small matched contained trial with cooling as a separate factor. Choose only the lowest total trip cost and carry-burden exact snack path that clears identity, ingredient, allergen, storage, seal, mess, texture, waste and route-exposure thresholds. Otherwise use an already proven route-and-lot control or defer carrying that sweet in those conditions. Do not issue a universal heat-resistance, health, food-safety or brand-winner verdict.

Preserve the exact seller fields and unknown labels, distinguish crystalline melting from sugar-glass and humidity failure, verify the current physical package, instrument the actual route, and choose only the lowest-total-trip-cost and carry-burden exact path that passes the matched contained trial; otherwise use a proven control or defer.

Do not name a summer-proof brand from form or marketing alone. Verify identity, ingredients, allergens, storage and seals, measure the pannier and backpack exposure, test small matched contained samples with cooling separate, then select the least burdensome passing path or defer.

The packet has four frozen seller pages, eight general concept pages and three scoped community discussions, but lacks complete current physical labels for all exact offers and a matched instrumented pannier and backpack exposure trial for the intended route, lot, weather, position, humidity, packaging and duration.

The four seller snapshots establish frozen price, rating, pack, mass, form and marketing fields but do not measure melting, softening, leakage, wrapper adhesion, texture or safety on the intended hot route.
Each displayed rating must stay paired with its review count, and neither a percentage nor the absence of reviews measures hot pannier or backpack portability.
A colorful candy shell or chocolatey-coating phrase does not identify an exact fat system, crystal state, melting range or higher heat tolerance.
Generic melting, polymorphism and compound-chocolate pages explain possible crystalline and coating mechanisms but do not assign an exact SKU threshold, thermal history or route result.

Hard candy can fail through material-specific glass softening, stickiness or environmental moisture uptake rather than classic crystalline melting, yet the background supplies no exact Skittles or Jolly Rancher threshold.
Shelf-stable describes sealed room-temperature storage achieved through product and packaging controls, not guaranteed texture, wrapper integrity or safety after uncontrolled heat or seal damage.
The sweat-sogged candy, old large cooler and disputed salt-and-ice comments motivate controls but cannot establish performance for any captured snack, small bag or route.

Physical identity, ingredients, allergens, filling, storage instructions, lot, net quantity, seal and wrapper integrity, delivered cost and intended serving must be verified before testing or recommending an exact item.
A roughly 90-degree ambient statement is not an internal exposure measurement; pannier and backpack temperature, humidity, sun, shade, duration, position and handling must be logged.

Insulation or an ice pack must be tested as a separate predeclared factor while recording start temperature, added mass, condensation and reusable-pack burden instead of attributing the effect to brand.

Small identified-lot samples in identical leakproof secondary containment must be matched on start temperature, bag position, route, duration and handling with predeclared leak, wrapper, shape, texture, consumption, waste and clean-up criteria; results remain local to tested conditions.

Choose only the lowest-total-trip-cost and carry-burden exact path clearing label, safety, packaging, mess, texture, waste and matched-exposure gates; otherwise use an already proven route-and-lot control or defer without a universal brand verdict.
The colorful shell proves that the captured M&M'S remains intact and safe in every 90-degree bag.
The word chocolatey proves that the exact Charleston Chew coating is compound chocolate with a known vegetable-fat formula.
Every compound coating has a higher melting point and better hot-route performance than every true chocolate.
A generic cocoa-butter table is the exact melting threshold of the captured M&M'S and Charleston Chew products.
The general polymorphism article identifies the crystal form and tempering history of both captured coated candies.
The 85-percent Jolly Rancher rating proves better hot-weather portability than the 73-percent M&M'S rating.
The absence of a posted Skittles or Charleston Chew review proves those products fail in heat.
The Skittles one-ounce product-dimensions field proves the total edible mass of all ninety packets.
Charleston Chew's frequently-enjoyed-frozen copy is a controlled hot-pannier performance test.
Hard candy cannot soften, stick, take up water or adhere to a wrapper under any summer condition.
Every amorphous candy has one universal glass-transition temperature that can be copied directly to both exact fruit candies.
The hygroscopy definition proves that these exact Skittles and Jolly Rancher lots fail at a specific humidity.
If a candy does not undergo crystalline melting, it cannot become sticky or unusable in a hot humid pack.
The workout story identifies one of the captured candies and proves its wrapper always becomes soggy.
A decades-old full-size Igloo cooler proves a small bicycle pannier with an ice pack will hold every snack cold for the intended trip.
The salt-and-ice thread contains a timed field experiment proving that salt makes a cooler stay cold longer on this route.
One fixed ice-pack mass is sufficient regardless of contents, starting temperature, insulation, ambient temperature or direct sun.
A 90-degree weather forecast is the exact internal temperature and humidity history of both bag positions.
Shelf-stable means the exact product is texture-stable and safe after any uncontrolled 90-degree exposure or broken seal.
Missing ingredients, allergens, filling and storage instructions may be inferred from the brand name and candy form.
The commuter may test an item before resolving its physical label, allergens, storage directions, filling and seal integrity.
Loose samples may be placed directly in different bag locations and any resulting mess attributed only to product identity.
One brand may receive an ice pack while another stays uncooled and the difference may still be called a brand effect.
One successful lot on one route proves the brand is universally summer-proof across weather, bags, positions and durations.
The lowest sticker price should be selected before verifying the current label, seal, delivered total and matched exposure result.
The selected path is therefore the universally safest and most heat-resistant sweet brand.
Shape retention and acceptable texture alone establish universal food safety after hot exposure.
A recommendation must name one of the four products even when every exact path has unresolved safety or exposure cells.

research_subgoals.description: Audit the four exact seller snapshots, preserve price, rating denominator, pack, mass, form and packaging ambiguity, and state why none is a hot-route measurement.
Explain crystalline melting, polymorphism and compound coating while refusing to assign an exact SKU fat identity, crystal form, threshold or heat advantage.
Explain hard-candy formulation, glass transition and humidity uptake as distinct possible failure paths without turning them or the sweat anecdote into an exact-product threshold.
Separate route exposure, passive containment and active cooling, and keep the sweat, old-cooler and salt-and-ice discussions at their exact anecdotal scope.
Combine all branches into a current physical-label and seal gate, instrumented pannier and backpack profiles, and a small matched leakproof trial with cooling separate and predeclared outcomes.
Choose only the lowest-total-trip-cost and carry-burden exact path that clears every gate, otherwise use a proven route-and-lot control or defer without universal heat, safety or brand claims.

query_requirements.text: Audit all four exact offers and preserve each frozen price, rating and review count, pack, mass, form, wrapper or coating claim and unresolved physical-label field while separating seller assertions from measured hot-route performance.
Explain melting point, crystal polymorphism and compound coating only as general mechanisms and do not infer an exact product fat system, crystal history, melting range or heat superiority.

Explain hard candy, glass transition and hygroscopy as separate material mechanisms and do not assign an exact fruit-candy threshold or treat non-melting as proof against softening, sticking or moisture damage.

Keep the sweat-covered candy, old cooler and salt-and-ice discussions at their author, container, scale and condition scope, and use them only to motivate measurement, containment and cooling controls.

Verify the current physical identity, ingredients, allergens, filling, storage directions, lot, net quantity and seals, measure actual pannier and backpack exposure, and specify a small matched leakproof route trial with cooling separate and predeclared mess, texture, consumption, waste and burden outcomes.

Select only the lowest-total-trip-cost and carry-burden exact path passing every current-label, safety, packaging and matched-exposure gate; otherwise use a proven route-and-lot control or defer without a universal brand or food-safety verdict.
